messages:
maria: Heads up — after landing the adaptive-kernel-selector change (commit abc123) I started seeing a p99 tail spike for streaming responses when we use small chunk flush intervals. Repro on staging with microbatch=8, streaming_chunk_tokens=8, flush_interval=40ms. p50 stays fine but p99 jumps ~180ms.

devon: interesting. do you see any KV-cache churn around that time? could be cache misses causing dm-kernel fallbacks.

maria: yes, KV miss rate edges up when concurrency > 120. profiler shows a cluster of "kernel_init" + "memcpy_h2d" at the tail. looks like kernel selection might be picking a slower path for short sequences, then we pay init + memcpy each time.

oliver: can you paste the small profiler trace? even a cropped stack would help.

maria: pasted below (sanitized):
```
1500ms request start
  20ms first token emit
  40ms small kernel matmul_v1 init
  65ms memcpy h2d (kv miss)
  90-110ms token compute
  180ms final chunk flush
```
Not perfect formatting but you get the idea.

harpreet: that lines up with what I saw — adaptive selector prefers "matmul_v1" for short seqs to save FLOPs, but for streaming with many tiny chunks the kernel init cost dominates. So throughput-optimal choice becomes latency-harmful at p99.

maria: exactly. sample numbers: with streaming_chunk=8 + flush=40ms + microbatch=8 we get throughput ~120 reqs/s, p95=70ms, p99=185ms. Increasing flush to 120ms: throughput up to 170 reqs/s, p95=95ms, p99 drops to 130ms (weird but consistent).

devon: weird that p95 increased with larger flush. probably because batching becomes more effective but average waiting per token increases. p99 improved because fewer kernel inits and fewer KV thrashes.

perf-bot: CI perf test failed: streaming_latency_p99 increased by 22% on canary after abc123. Linked run: ci/reports/7890

maria: I ran an experiment with hybrid-flush: send first chunk immediately (flush=0ms for first chunk) then aggregate following chunks with flush=80ms to allow batching. results: p50 ~ lower, p95 ~ similar, p99 down ~40ms. So perceived latency for first-token improved without killing throughput.

oliver: nice. code sketch?

maria:
```python
# pseudocode
def on_new_request(req):
    send_chunk(req.first_tokens, immediate=True)
    start_timer(req, interval=steady_flush)

# steady_flush = 80ms, immediate first chunk to reduce time-to-first-byte
```

harpreet: that helps UX but we still have the kernel-selection mismatch. propose we change selector to prefer "warm" kernels (ones with low init and low memcpy) when stream_mode==true and chunk_size small. fallback: keep current selector for bulk batch mode.

devon: +1. also want to try adaptive microbatch sizing: when streaming and active concurrency high, reduce microbatch to 4 to avoid long queuing for first chunks, or conversely bump it when flush grows to benefit from batching. Tradeoffs obvious but we should quantify.

maria: I ran microbatch sweep: microbatch=1,4,8,16 with chunk=8/flush=40ms. microbatch=1 gives best p50/p95 but terrible throughput (40 req/s). 4 seems sweet spot: p95 <100ms and throughput ~110 req/s. 8 is our default currently — too batchy for tiny-chunk streaming.

perf-bot: uploaded perf traces: s3://redwood-ci/streams/1777004321/trace.zip

devon: another angle: KV cache eviction policy. when many concurrent short streams, KV cache entries are tiny and turnover is high. If we prioritize hot session pins (LRU->pin for active streams) we could reduce h2d memcpys. Any objections?

oliver: agree. can we implement a lightweight session pin expiry (e.g., pin active stream keys for 200ms after last access)? pins cheap but should cut reupload.

harpreet: one caveat: pins increase memory footprint. need to add a heuristic: pin if session qps > X and model_kv_size < Y.

maria: noted. I'll open a PR for: 1) kernel selector tweak for stream/small-chunk mode, 2) hybrid flush default (first chunk immediate), 3) session pin heuristic, 4) microbatch auto-tuner experiment.

devon: for the PR add a perf dashboard comparing p50/p95/p99 + throughput across the sweeps. keep current selector behind a feature flag for canary.

maria: will do. tagging for followups: @harpreet for KV pin design, @oliver for selector logic, @devon for microbatch tuner.

ci-bot: Created ticket INF-2437: "streaming: reduce tail latency for small chunks" and linked PR #4512.

maria: thanks. will run end-to-end canary with hybrid flush + selector flag tomorrow morning and post results. :rocket: 

oliver: cool — if you need extra GPUs ping me, I'll carve out time.

harpreet: I'll prototype pinning tonight and post a microbenchmark. :coffee:

maria: perfect, closing loop here. will update thread with numbers. :white_check_mark:
